verses.zh: 十一年三月初一日，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month,[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要向埃及王法老和他的众人说：在威势上谁能与你相比呢？
verses.en: “Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and his hordes:“‘Who are you like in your greatness?

verses.zh: 亚述王曾如黎巴嫩中的香柏树，枝条荣美，影密如林，极其高大，树尖插入云中。
verses.en: Consider Assyria,[NOTE:1] a cedar in Lebanon,[NOTE:2] with beautiful branches, like a forest giving shade,and extremely tall;its top reached into the clouds.
notes: Either Egypt or the Lord compares Egypt to Assyria, which is described in vv. 3-17 through the metaphor of a majestic tree. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:185. Like Egypt, Assyria had been a great world power, but in time God brought the Assyrians down. Egypt should learn from history the lesson that no nation, no matter how powerful, can withstand the judgment of God. Rather than following the text here, some prefer to emend the proper name Assyria to a similar sounding common noun meaning “boxwood” (see Ezek 27:6), which would make a fitting parallel to “cedar of Lebanon” in the following line. In this case vv. 3-18 in their entirety refer to Egypt, not Assyria. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:121-27.
Lebanon was known for its cedar trees (Judg 9:15; 1 Kgs 4:33; 5:6; 2 Kgs 14:9; Ezra 3:7; Pss 29:5; 92:12; 104:16).

verses.zh: 众水使它生长；深水使它长大。所栽之地有江河围流，汊出的水道延到田野诸树。
verses.en: The water made it grow;underground springs made it grow tall.Rivers flowed all around the place it was planted,while smaller channels watered all the trees of the field.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Waters made it grow; the deep made it grow tall. It [the deep] was flowing with its rivers around the place it [the tree] was planted. It [the deep] sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.”

verses.zh: 所以他高大超过田野诸树；发旺的时候，枝子繁多，因得大水之力枝条长长。
verses.en: Therefore it grew taller than all the trees of the field;its boughs grew large and its branches grew long,because of the plentiful water in its shoots.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “when it sends forth.” Repointing the consonants of the Masoretic text would render the proposed reading of “shoots” (cf. NRSV).

verses.zh: 空中的飞鸟都在枝子上搭窝；田野的走兽都在枝条下生子；所有大国的人民都在它荫下居住。
verses.en: All the birds of the sky nested in its boughs;under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth;in its shade all the great[NOTE:1] nations lived.

verses.zh: 树大条长，成为荣美，因为根在众水之旁。
verses.en: It was beautiful in its loftiness, in the length of its branches;for its roots went down deep to plentiful waters.

verses.zh: 神园中的香柏树不能遮蔽它；松树不及它的枝子；枫树不及它的枝条；　神园中的树都没有它荣美。
verses.en: The cedars in the garden of God could not eclipse it,nor could the fir trees[NOTE:1] match its boughs;the plane trees were as nothing compared to its branches;no tree in the garden of God could rival its beauty.
notes: Or “cypress trees” (cf. NASB, NLT); NIV84 “pine trees”; NIV11 “junipers.”

verses.zh: 我使它的枝条蕃多，成为荣美，以致　神伊甸园中的树都嫉妒它。」
verses.en: I made it beautiful with its many branches;all the trees of Eden, in the garden of God, envied it.

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：「因它高大，树尖插入云中，心骄气傲，
verses.en: “‘Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because it was tall in stature, and its top reached into the clouds, and it was proud of its height,

verses.zh: 我就必将他交给列国中大有威势的人；他必定办他。我因他的罪恶，已经驱逐他。
verses.en: I gave it over to the leader of the nations. He has judged it thoroughly,[NOTE:1] as its sinfulness deserves. I have thrown it out.
notes: Heb “acting he has acted with regard to it.” The infinitive absolute precedes the main verb to emphasize the certainty and decisiveness of the action depicted.

verses.zh: 外邦人，就是列邦中强暴的，将它砍断弃掉。它的枝条落在山间和一切谷中，它的枝子折断，落在地的一切河旁。地上的众民已经走去，离开它的荫下。
verses.en: Foreigners from the most terrifying nations have cut it down and left it to lie there on the mountains. In all the valleys its branches have fallen, and its boughs lie broken in the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the land[NOTE:1] have departed[NOTE:2] from its shade and left it.

verses.zh: 空中的飞鸟都要宿在这败落的树上，田野的走兽都要卧在它的枝条下，
verses.en: On its ruins all the birds of the sky will live, and all the wild animals[NOTE:1] will walk[NOTE:2] on its branches.
notes: Heb “the beasts of the field,” referring to wild as opposed to domesticated animals.

verses.zh: 好使水旁的诸树不因高大而自尊，也不将树尖插入云中，并且那些得水滋润、有势力的，也不得高大自立。因为它们在世人中，和下坑的人都被交与死亡，到阴府去了。」
verses.en: For this reason no watered trees will grow so tall; their tops will not reach into the clouds, nor will the well-watered ones grow that high.[NOTE:1] For all of them have been appointed to die in the lower parts of the earth;[NOTE:2] they will be among mere mortals,[NOTE:3] with those who descend to the Pit.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and they will not stand to them in their height, all the drinkers of water.”
Heb “for death, to the lower earth.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「它下阴间的那日，我便使人悲哀。我为它遮盖深渊，使江河凝结，大水停流；我也使黎巴嫩为它凄惨，田野的诸树都因它发昏。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: On the day it[NOTE:1] went down to Sheol I caused observers to lament.[NOTE:2] I covered it with the deep and held back its rivers; its plentiful water was restrained. I clothed Lebanon in black for it, and all the trees of the field wilted because of it.
notes: Heb “I caused lamentation.” D. I. Block (Ezekiel [NICOT], 2:194-95) proposes an alternative root that would give the meaning: “I gated back the waters,” i.e., shut off the water supply.
For the expression “going down to the Pit,” see Ezek 26:20 and 32:18, 24, 29.

verses.zh: 我将它扔到阴间，与下坑的人一同下去。那时，列国听见它坠落的响声就都震动，并且伊甸的一切树―就是黎巴嫩得水滋润、最佳最美的树―都在阴府受了安慰。
verses.en: I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when I threw it down to Sheol, along with those who descend to the Pit.[NOTE:1] Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and the best of Lebanon, all that were well-watered, were comforted in the earth below.

verses.zh: 它们也与它同下阴间，到被杀的人那里。它们曾作它的膀臂，在列国中它的荫下居住。
verses.en: Those who lived in its shade, its allies[NOTE:1] among the nations, also went down with it to Sheol, to those killed by the sword.

verses.zh: 在这样荣耀威势上，在伊甸园诸树中，谁能与你相比呢？然而你要与伊甸的诸树一同下到阴府，在未受割礼的人中，与被杀的人一同躺卧。法老和他的群众乃是如此。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: Which of the trees of Eden was like you in majesty and loftiness? You will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lower parts of the earth; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword! This is what will happen to Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Third paragraph, etc.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 31:1-9

1In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the word of the Lord came to me saying, 2"Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his hordes,

'Whom are you like in your greatness?

3Behold, Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon

With beautiful branches and forest shade,

And very high, And its top was among the clouds.

4The waters made it grow, the deep made it high.

With its rivers it continually extended all around its planting

place,

And sent out its channels to all the trees of the field.

5Therefore its height was loftier than all the trees of the field

And its boughs became many and its branches long

Because of many waters as it spread them out.

6All the birds of the heavens nested in its boughs,

And under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth,

And all great nations lived under its shade.

7So it was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches;

For its roots extended to many waters.

8The cedars in God's garden could not match it;

The cypresses could not compare with its boughs,

And the plane trees could not match its branches.

No tree in God's garden could compare with it in its beauty.

9I made it beautiful with the multitude of its branches,

And all the trees of Eden, which were in the garden of God, were jealous of it.'"

31:1 See note at Ezek. 29:1. The date is 587 B.C.

31:2-3 "say to Pharaoh. . ." The literary unit dealing with YHWH's judgment on Egypt began in chapter 29 and continues
through chapter 32. Therefore, it is surprising to have "Assyria" addressed in Ezek. 31:3. Assyria is mentioned in Ezek. 32:22-33.
There are two options.

- Pharaoh is to view YHWH's judgment on Assyria (i.e. a tall tree, cf. Isa. 2:13; 10:18-19) as an example of what will befall him and
his nation (Jewish Study Bible, p. 1101 and NET Bible, p. 1512, #3).

- The Hebrew text, אשור (BDB 78), is corrupt and must be emended to

- "I will liken you to a cedar" (RSV), שור (BDB 1003 II, Qal
IMPERFECT plus "cedar," BDB 72)

- a variant spelling of "cypress" (i.e. "box-wood," type of cedar, אשׁור, BDB 81, KB 1677, cf. Ezek. 27:6)

The UBS Text Project, p. 101, gives "Assyria, a cedar" an "A" rating.

- Assyria, אתור (BDB 78)

- a cedar, תאשׁור (BDB 81)

Another word for "cedar" appears after "Assyria" in the MT, which is
spelled ארז (BDB 72), see 2,a, above.

31:3-9 The nation (i.e. I think this whole context is about Egypt, not Assyria) is described as

- beautiful branches for shade

- very tall (i.e. MT, NKJV, Peshitta, "among thick boughs' LXX, NRSV, NET, "among the clouds")

- deep roots into good water

- watered other trees

- protection for many animals (i.e. nations)

- greater than the trees of Eden

- many branches

In essence this is the "global/cosmic tree" imagery (cf. Psalm 80; Daniel 4). Trees were places
of special reverence and respect. They often served as holy sites (e.g. Gen. 35:4,8; Josh. 24:26; palm tree,
Jdg. 4:5; oaks of Ophrah, cf. Jdg. 6:11,19; 1 Kgs. 13:14; 1 Chr. 10:12) and also sites of fertility worship
(e.g. 1 Kgs. 14:23-24; Hosea 4:13). However, this cosmic tree symbolized a universal motif. It, of course, is a hyperbole
in this context describing Egypt (see note at Ezek. 31:2-3). YHWH allows nations to rise and He causes nations to fall (i.e. Jer. 1:10; 18:2-9).

In YHWH's garden His trees continue to grow and bear fruit (cf. Ezek. 47:12; Rev. 22:2). Heaven is symbolized
as a beautiful, fruitful garden (cf. Genesis 2 and Revelation 22).

Special Topic: Trees

Special Topic: Eden

31:4 "the deep" This is the Hebrew term tehom (BDB 1062, KB 1690) personified (cf. v. 15). See full note online
at Gen. 1:2, "the deep."

Special Topic: ANE Creation and Flood Myths

Special Topic: Waters

31:8

NASB, NJB, JPSOA
"cypresses"

NKJV, NRSV, TEV
"fir trees"

REB, NASB margin
"juniper"

LXX, NEB
"pines"

The UBS, Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 162-163, identifies this (BDB 141) as an
Aleppo pine, which is the largest conifer in the Mediterranean area. They can reach over 50' in height.
Its wood is hard enough to use as building material (cf. 1 Kgs. 5:8,10; 6:15,34; 2 Chr. 2:8; Isa. 14:8;
Ezek. 27:5; 31:8). It is used to characterize a nation in Hosea 14:8; Zech. 11:1-3.

NASB, NRSV, TEV, REB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"the plane trees"

NKJV
"the chestnut trees"

LXX
"silver firs"

The UBS, Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 166-167, calls this a "plane tree." The Hebrew
(BDB 790) root means "stripped" of bark (cf. Gen. 30:37). It is native to Palestine and grows near a water source. They are large and long-lived.

31:9 "Eden" Eden is a geographical location (i.e. in Ugaritic, "a plain") in Genesis 2-3 which contained a special garden
planted and prepared by God for His highest creation (i.e. made in God's image and likeness, cf. Gen. 1:26-27), mankind (cf. Gen. 2:8).

The special garden is alluded to in Isa. 51:3; Ezek. 28:13; 31:9,16,18(twice); 36:35; and Joel 2:3.

Apparently the word means "abundance" from an Aramaic root. In Hebrew (BDB 727 III, 792 II) the root means "delight"
or "pleasure." After Genesis the term is imagery for a well watered, fruitful place.

Special Topic: Eden

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 31:10-14

10'Therefore thus says the Lord God, "Because it is high in
stature and has set its top among the clouds, and its heart is haughty in its loftiness, 11therefore I will give it into the hand of a despot of the
nations; he will thoroughly deal with it. According to its wickedness I have driven it away. 12Alien tyrants of the nations have cut it down and left it;
on the mountains and in all the valleys its branches have fallen and its boughs have been broken in all the ravines of the land. And all the peoples of the earth
have gone down from its shade and left it. 13On its ruin all the birds of the heavens will dwell, and all the beasts of the field will be on its fallen
branches 14so that all the trees by the waters may not be exalted in their stature, nor set their top among the clouds, nor their well-watered mighty
ones stand erect in their height. For they have all been given over to death, to the earth beneath, among the sons of men, with those who go down to the pit."

31:10 Again, like Tyre (i.e. Ezek. 28:2,17), Assyria (cf. Isa. 10:12), and Babylon (cf. Isa. 14:11-14; Dan. 4:30; 5:20-23), the sin
which caused YHWH to act was pride, arrogance, hubris! It is the essence of self-centeredness. It is the fruit of Eden (see Special Topic: The Fall of Mankind).
Maybe this is why Ezekiel uses the Garden of Eden imagery to characterize

- Tyre, Ezek. 28

- Egypt, Ezek. 31

The word "greatness" or "magnify" (BDB 152) is most often used of YHWH (e.g. Deut. 3:24; 5:24; 9:26; 11:2; 32:3;
Ezek. 38:23), but here it is used of human pride.

- Israel, Isa. 9:9

- Assyria, Isa. 10:12

- Egypt, Ezek. 31:2,7,8,18

- Edom, Ezek. 35:13

- Moab, Jer. 48:26,42

- the king, Dan. 11:36-37

31:11

NASB
"despot of the nations"

NKJV
"the most terrible of the nations"

LXX, NRSV, NJB, REB
"the presence of the nations"

TEV
"a foreign ruler"

JPSOA
"the mightiest of the nations"

Peshitta
"the mighty one of the nations"

The MT has a CONSTRUCT of BDB 18 and 156 ("a mighty one of the nations"). The key
term (BDB 18, KB 40) means "leader," "chief," originally "ram." The same term is used of the tree in Ezek. 31:14 (cf. Isa. 1:27-31).

▣ "he will thoroughly deal with it" This is an INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and an IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root (BDB 793, KB 889), which denotes intensity or completeness. This refers to YHWH's agent of judgment on Egypt.

▣ "I have driven it away" This same VERB (BDB 176, KB 204, Piel PERFECT) was used

- of Adam and Eve being driven from Eden (cf. Gen. 3:24)

- of Cain (cf. Gen. 4:14)

- of Egypt exiled from her homeland by YHWH

31:12 "alien tyrants of the nations" This is the same phrase that is used in Ezek. 28:7; 30:11; 32:12 to
refer to the army of Nebuchadnezzar II, king of Neo-Babylon.

▣ "all the peoples of the earth have gone down from its shade" This is typical prophetic hyperbole.
Egypt did have many allies and many mercenaries in her army (cf. Ezek. 31:12-13).

31:14 The destruction of Assyria, Tyre, Egypt, and later Neo-Babylon itself should be a graphic warning to
other prideful, power-hungry nations (cf. Ezek. 31:15-18). Death finally sends all fallen humans to their
grave (i.e. "to the earth beneath. . .those who go down to the pit").

Special Topic: Where Are the Dead?

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 31:15-17

15'Thus says the Lord God, "On the day when it went down to Sheol I
caused lamentations; I closed the deep over it and held back its rivers. And its many waters were stopped up, and I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all the
trees of the field wilted away on account of it. 16I made the nations quake at the sound of its fall when I made it go down to Sheol with those who go
down to the pit; and all the well-watered trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, were comforted in the earth beneath. 17They also went down
with it to Sheol to those who were slain by the sword; and those who were its strength lived under its shade among the nations."

31:15-18 This paragraph mixes imageries.

- Sheol (i.e. "the deep"), Ezek. 31:15-18 (cf. Isa. 14:8-11; see Special Topic: Sheol, I. B.)

- Egypt as a river nation (i.e. "held back its rivers"), Ezek. 31:15

- Lebanon darkened, Ezek. 31:15

- all the trees of the field wilt away, Ezek. 31:15,16b

The trees of Eden and Lebanon are parallel and represent nations. There is a recurrent play on water
in this paragraph.

- the deep, Ezek. 31:15

- rivers, Ezek. 31:15

- many waters

- drinkers of water (i.e. trees of Eden), Ezek. 31:16

Special Topic: Waters

31:16 "I made. . ." The NASB repeats this VERB twice, but in the MT it is two VERBS.

- BDB 950, KB 1271, Hiphil PERFECT

- BDB 432, KB 434, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT,
cf. Ezek. 26:20

Both of these VERBS show the sovereign actions of YHWH. He sets up nations; He humbles nations. All history is in His hand.

Notice the three "I" VERBS of Ezek. 31:15.

▣ "go down to the pit" This idiom is found in Ezek. 26:20; 32:18,24,29. It denotes Sheol, which refers to the
holding place of the dead until judgment day (see Special Topic: Sheol, I. B.)

The question is, "Are there levels of Sheol?"

- Ezek. 26:20, "the lower parts of the earth"

- Ezek. 31:18, "in the midst of the uncircumcised"

The first is simply a parallel, but the second may denote a worse place (cf. Ezek. 28:10; 32:24,29,30).

Special Topic: Degrees of Rewards and Punishment

31:17

NASB
"those who were its strength"

NKJV
"those who were its strong arm"

NRSV, NET
"its allies" (cf. v. 6)

NJB
"its offspring"

REB
"those among the nations"

JPSOA
"its supporters"

LXX
"his seed"

Peshitta
"its posterity"

The MT has "and his arm" (BDB 283). The LXX, Peshitta, and NJB assume the same consonants but different vowels, "seed" (BDB282).

The UBS Text Project, p. 104, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

▣ "lived under its shade" See Special Topic: Shadow As a Metaphor for Protection and Care

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 31:18

18"To which among the trees of
Eden are you thus equal in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the earth beneath; you will lie in the midst of the uncircumcised,
with those who were slain by the sword. So is Pharaoh and all his hordes!'" declares the Lord God."

31:18 The prophet is addressing Egypt in terms that described her greatness. Now he asks Egypt, are you a
great tree also? YHWH will cut down Assyria, Egypt, and later Neo-Babylon.

▣ "the uncircumcised" See note at Ezek. 28:10.

Special Topic: Circumcision

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did Ezekiel use metaphors from the Garden of Eden?

- What is the symbol of a cosmic tree?

- How do the metaphors of Ezek. 31 affect one's interpretation of Ezekiel 28?
